## A small, complete example

Code is part of the argument. **IBM Plex Mono** gives it a distinct voice,
with readable `0O`, `1Il`, `{}[]()`, and `=> != <=` at a practical size.
The font files ship with the theme, so they work without a font service.

```{.python filename="catalog.py"}
from dataclasses import dataclass
from pathlib import Path

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Book:
    title: str
    author: str
    year: int

def find_books(books: list[Book], query: str) -> list[Book]:
    """Find a title or author, ignoring case."""
    needle = query.casefold()
    return [
        book for book in books
        if needle in f"{book.title} {book.author}".casefold()
    ]

books = [Book("A Room with a View", "E. M. Forster", 1908)]
print(find_books(books, "forster"))  # One good place to begin
```

## More than one language

::: {.panel-tabset}

### Python

```python
titles = [book.title for book in books if book.year < 1920]
for title in sorted(titles):
    print(title)
```

### JavaScript

```javascript
const titles = books
  .filter(book => book.year < 1920)
  .map(book => book.title)
  .sort();
console.log(titles);
```

### SQL

```sql
SELECT title, author
FROM books
WHERE year < 1920
ORDER BY title;
```

:::

## Details when you need them

<details class="code-fold">
<summary>Show the validation example</summary>

```python
def validate(book: Book) -> None:
    if not book.title.strip():
        raise ValueError("A book needs a title")
    if book.year < 1:
        raise ValueError("The year must be positive")
```

</details>
